full_article: In this debate on India Today's prime-time show, host Preeti Choudhry leads a discussion on the eight course corrections initiated by the Election Commission of India over five weeks following media reports alleging irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process. Former Chief Election Commissioner OP Rawat describes these actions as merely a 'damage control exercise' and calls on the three election commissioners to hold a joint media conference to address doubts, clarify procedures, and protect the credibility of the institution. Bharatiya Janata Party spokesperson Radhika Khera defends the poll body, asserting that the Election Commission is a responsive and dynamic institution adapting to an electorate exceeding 140 crore. Congress spokesperson Advocate Arshdeep Khadial counters that the repeated rectifications represent admissions of wrongdoing, pointing to protests and court petitions challenging modifications to Form 6 and voter deletions. The panel also debates RTI findings detailing communications sent to the Cabinet Secretary.

title: Vikram Misri Holds High-Level Talks In Nepal Ahead Of PM Shah’s India Visit - News Mobile
description: Vikram Misri Holds High-Level Talks In Nepal Ahead Of PM Shah’s India Visit  News Mobile
publisher.title: News Mobile
full_article:
Kathmandu: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri held a series of high-level meetings with Nepalese leaders during his two-day official visit to Nepal, reviewing bilateral cooperation across various sectors and discussing possible outcomes and initiatives ahead of Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s upcoming visit to India.

According to a joint press release issued by India’s Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and Nepal’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday, Misri visited Nepal on November 4-5 at the invitation of Nepalese Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai.

During the visit, Misri called on Prime Minister Balendra Shah and conveyed greetings from Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The two discussed progress in bilateral cooperation and preparations for Shah’s upcoming visit to India.

Misri highlighted the “wide-ranging engagement and overall progress in diverse areas of bilateral cooperation” and discussed possible outcomes and initiatives in the context of the Nepalese Prime Minister’s visit to India.

He also met Nepal’s Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal, Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha, and Minister for Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal.

On Wednesday, Misri and Nepalese Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai held delegation-level talks, reviewing ongoing cooperation across various sectors and discussing ways to strengthen the mutually beneficial partnership between the two countries.

Misri also interacted with parliamentarians, including members of the India-Nepal Parliamentary Friendship Group and Nepal’s Parliamentary Committee on International Relations and Tourism.

According to the joint release, Nepalese leaders expressed gratitude for India’s “swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance” following the Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi floods.

Both sides noted growing engagement in traditional areas of cooperation, including trade and commerce, development partnership, hydropower, physical connectivity, border management, energy and people-to-people ties.

The discussions also covered newer areas of collaboration, including start-ups, digital connectivity, artificial intelligence (AI) and sports.

“Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to all round enhancement of the bilateral partnership,” the joint press release stated.

The visit continued the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries to advance their close bilateral ties of friendship and cooperation.

title: Police Seize Ganja, Heroin In Two Separate Operations Near India-Nepal Border - Rediff
description: Police Seize Ganja, Heroin In Two Separate Operations Near India-Nepal Border  Rediff
publisher.title: Rediff
full_article:
Authorities have made significant arrests and seizures of ganja and heroin in two separate operations near the India-Nepal border, highlighting ongoing efforts to combat cross-border drug trafficking.

IMAGE: This is an AI-generated image and has been used only for representational purposes.

Key Points Two individuals were arrested on Thursday with approximately 123 kg of ganja, valued at Rs 60 lakh, near the India-Nepal border in Maharajganj.

The ganja seizure operation involved Thuthibari police and ATS units, leading to the arrest of Naimun Nisha and Rajendra Gaur.

Separately, a 19-year-old Nepal national, Rohit Maurya, was apprehended on November 4 with 57.24 grams of heroin near the international border.

Both operations resulted in cases registered under various sections of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act.

One of the accused, Rajendra Gaur, has two previous cases under the NDPS Act from 2020 and 2023.

Two persons were arrested with around 123 kg of ganja worth an estimated Rs 60 lakh in the international market, while a 19-year-old Nepal national was held with heroin in two separate operations near the India-Nepal border here, police said on Thursday.

Major Ganja Seizure Near India-Nepal Border

In the first operation, the Thuthibari police, along with the Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) units of Siddharthnagar and Gorakhpur, arrested two persons near Naubari village following a tip-off, Superintendent of Police Shakti Mohan Avasthy said.

The accused have been identified as Naimun Nisha alias Jahantara (49), a resident of Chainpatti village in Kushinagar district, and Rajendra Gaur alias Ravindra (50), a resident of Azad Nagar in the same district.

Police seized 122.975 kg of ganja and a Scorpio vehicle allegedly used for smuggling. Awasthy said the seized contraband was estimated to be worth Rs 60 lakh in the international market.

A case has been registered at Thuthibari police station under Sections 8, 20 and 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, and the accused are being produced before a court.

Police said Gaur has two previous cases under the NDPS Act registered against him, one in Kushinagar in 2020 and another in Basti district in 2023.

Nepal National Apprehended With Heroin

In the second operation, a joint team of Sonauli police and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB) personnel arrested a 19-year-old Nepal national with 57.24 grams of heroin near the international border on November 4.

The accused, identified as Rohit Maurya, a resident of Siddharthanagar municipality in Nepal's Rupandehi district, was apprehended near a primary school in Fareni village during a checking drive following a tip-off, police said.

A Nepal-registered motorcycle was also seized from his possession.

A case has been registered against Maurya at Sonauli police station under Sections 8, 21(b) and 23 of the NDPS Act. He was subsequently produced before a local court for further legal proceedings, police added.

Misri conveyed the message during a meeting with Prime Minister Shah at Singha Durbar, saying Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi was also looking forward to receiving his Nepali counterpart. Shah, in response, said preparations for his visit were underway.

According to Foreign Ministry officials, Shah is scheduled to visit India from November 23 to 25, with preparations being expedited on both sides. The three-day visit is expected to focus on strengthening bilateral ties and identifying priority areas for cooperation.

A meeting between Shah and Modi is being planned for November 23, although it could be pushed to the following day if scheduling constraints arise.

The government is also planning to keep the delegation relatively small, with discussions underway to limit its size to fewer than 15 members. The possibility of including private-sector representatives is also being considered.

Nepal’s Acting Ambassador to India, Surendra Thapa, has arrived in Kathmandu to coordinate preparations. He has held consultations with Foreign Ministry officials and other relevant agencies.

“Preparations are underway. Not everything has been finalised yet. We are working to conclude the remaining arrangements. Everything should become clear in a few days,” said Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Lok Bahadur Chhetri.

Shah is preparing to visit India nearly eight months after assuming office. The trip will mark his first major bilateral engagement with a neighbouring country as prime minister. Earlier, he travelled to the United States to attend the United Nations General Assembly, where he raised issues concerning climate justice and Nepal’s interests on the international stage.

Misri’s two-day visit to Nepal was largely focused on preparations for Shah’s upcoming India visit and broader bilateral cooperation. During his meeting with Shah on Thursday, Misri conveyed greetings from Modi and discussed possible outcomes and initiatives to be pursued during the Nepali prime minister’s visit, according to a joint statement issued by the two countries.

Misri also held meetings with Foreign Minister Khanal, Finance Minister Dr Swarnim Wagle, Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha, and Infrastructure Development Minister Sunil Lamsal.

During delegation-level talks with his Nepali counterpart Amrit Bahadur Rai, the two sides reviewed ongoing cooperation across various sectors and discussed ways to strengthen the bilateral partnership. He also interacted with parliamentarians, including members of the Nepal-India Parliamentary Friendship Group and the Parliamentary Committee on International Relations and Tourism.

The two sides expressed satisfaction with expanding cooperation in trade, development partnership, hydropower, physical connectivity, border management, energy and people-to-people relations. They also identified emerging areas for collaboration, including start-ups, digital connectivity, artificial intelligence and sports.

Notably, Misri’s itinerary did not include meetings with leaders of other opposition parties. His political engagements were limited to Prime Minister Shah, ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Chairman Rabi Lamichhane and Nepali Congress (NC) President Gagan Thapa, the main opposition leader.

During the meeting, Shah thanked India for its assistance following the devastating Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi floods in August. He specifically acknowledged India's role as the first responder including the supply of relief materials and deployment of rescue teams. Shah also thanked Modi for expressing solidarity with Nepal through a phone call following the disaster.

The Prime Minister also expressed interest in exploring cooperation with India for the development of sports in Nepal.

The Indian Foreign Secretary also met Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Infrastructure Development Minister Sunil Lamsal and ruling Rastriya Swatantra Party Chair Rabi Lamichhane. During the engagements, both sides discussed cooperation in trade, development partnership, hydropower, physical connectivity, border management and energy along with newer areas such as start-ups, digital connectivity, artificial intelligence and sports.

Focus on concrete outcomes

Kathmandu is preparing to ensure that the visit goes beyond formal meetings and traditional declarations with the government seeking tangible progress on issues that have remained unresolved for years.

Officials said the Prime Minister's Office and the Foreign Ministry had emphasised the need for thorough preparations, particularly on matters involving border disputes, existing bilateral agreements and their implementation.

Key areas expected to feature in discussions include the Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project, air connectivity, road and rail links, trade and transit arrangements and energy cooperation.

Nepal is also expected to raise the issue of additional air entry routes through India which Kathmandu has long sought to facilitate international flights and improve the utilisation of Gautam Buddha and Pokhara international airports.

Connectivity including Indian assistance in airport development and upgrading as well as road and rail links will also be among the proposed priorities.

Energy cooperation is another major area of focus particularly Indian investment in hydropower projects and access to the Indian electricity market. Nepal also wants to explore arrangements to export its electricity to third countries through the Indian market along with the infrastructure and policy support required.

Shah's proposed India visit comes around eight months after he became prime minister. It will be his first major bilateral visit to a neighbouring country as head of government.

He had earlier travelled to the United States to attend the United Nations General Assembly where he raised issues of climate justice and Nepal's concerns on the international stage.

description: Nepal Team Briefs Rabi Lamichhane on COP-31 Preparations and Priorities  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. A team including the minister representing Nepal in the 31st Conference of the Parties (COP-31) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) has met with Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) Chairman Rabi Lamichhane to provide information about the conference preparations and Nepal's priorities.

A team including Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Minister for Agriculture, Forest and Environment Gita Chaudhary, Members of Parliament, and climate experts met with Chairman Lamichhane today to provide information and discuss the government's preparations for the conference to be held in Antalya, Turkey from November 9 to 20.

On the occasion, Chairman Lamichhane urged for a strong presence at the COP-31 conference, for everyone to play their role, and to inform the international community about the impacts of climate change faced by Nepal.

During the meeting, Minister Chaudhary provided information about Nepal's participation in the conference, national preparations, the delegation's structure, and the main agendas that Nepal will advance in climate diplomacy, according to her secretariat.

The discussion included information about Nepal's national priorities at COP-31, climate risks in the Himalayan region, climate justice, climate finance, and Nepal's stance on adaptation issues and the achievements sought from the conference.

Minister Chaudhary informed that Nepal is preparing to prioritize issues such as further commitment from developed nations on emission reduction at COP-31, easy and predictable climate finance and technology transfer for least developed and Himalayan countries, and inclusion of the Himalayas in the formal agenda of the conference.

Similarly, Advisor to Minister Chaudhary, Abhishek Shrestha, informed that Nepal's preparations include placing Himalayan issues on the priority of international climate negotiations through the joint initiative of Nepal and Bhutan, addressing the relationship between melting glaciers and rising sea levels through regional cooperation and early warning systems, and emphasizing the effective implementation of finance related to loss and damage and adaptation.

The Government of Nepal has organized a National Climate Summit and prepared Nepal's concept paper for COP-31. This concept paper includes suggestions received from various government bodies, provincial and local levels, development partners, civil society, academia, and the private sector.

Foreign Minister Khanal will lead Nepal's delegation to COP-31. Nepal is preparing to raise issues of Himalayan conservation, climate adaptation, climate finance, and climate justice with the international community at the conference.

title: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit - The Hindu
description: Foreign Secretary Misri sets stage for Nepal PM’s upcoming India visit  The Hindu
publisher.title: The Hindu
full_article:
Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri on Thursday (November 5, 2026) met Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah in Kathmandu, with discussions focused on “possible outcomes and initiatives” from the expected upcoming visit of the Himalayan nation’s leader to New Delhi.

Concluding his official engagements in Nepal that spanned Wednesday and Thursday, Mr. Misri also met Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal.

“The Foreign Secretary of India highlighted the wide-ranging engagement and overall progress in diverse areas of bilateral cooperation, and discussed possible outcomes and initiatives in the context of the upcoming visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal to India,” stated a joint press release issued by the Ministry of External Affairs and Kathmandu’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

A shared disaster, beyond borders and geopolitics

Mr. Misri held detailed talks with his host, Nepali Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai, on the “mutually beneficial partnership” between India and Nepal.

Mr. Shah had earlier this year highlighted the border dispute with India in the Lipulekh-Kalapai-Limpiyadhura area that is part of India’s Uttarakhand but claimed by Nepal as a sticking point in ties.

Nepal has also encroached upon Indian territory, says PM Balendra Shah

Mr. Shah had sought to involve other countries, such as the United Kingdom and China, in talks on the issue. But India wants the matter to be resolved bilaterally.

The Nepali leaders expressed “gratitude for India’s swift and substantial humanitarian and technical assistance in the aftermath of the Bhotekoshi floods”, the joint press release stated.

Mr. Misri’s discussions with Nepali stakeholders included a “commerce and development partnership, hydropower, physical connectivity, border management, energy and people-to-people ties”, as well as new areas like digital connectivity and AI.

Mr. Misri also met Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and Minister for Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal.

Mr. Shah was sworn in as Prime Minister in March this year following the Gen-Z uprising in Nepal in September 2025 that led to the ouster of the previous government.

description: Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri Concludes Two-Day Nepal Visit  Ratopati
publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article:
Kathmandu. India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri has returned to his country. He returned after completing a two-day official visit to Nepal at the invitation of Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai.

During the visit, Indian Secretary Misri also met with Chairman of the Rastriya Swatantra Party Rabi Lamichhane on his way out. In the meeting, Chairman Lamichhane discussed his past official visit to India and the reception given by India.

He extended best wishes for the success of the high-level visits to be held between the two countries in the coming days. He extended best wishes for the success of Prime Minister Balen's upcoming visit to India. He expressed the view that Nepal is emphasizing development and economic diplomacy between the two countries. Discussions were also held on further strengthening the relationship between the two countries.

There was no program to meet with leaders of political parties. In the end, he met with Chairman Lamichhane on his way out and returned. He also held a meeting with Prime Minister Balendra Shah. During the meeting, Secretary Misri handed over a goodwill message on behalf of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that he provided information about the progress made in the multifaceted relationship and various areas of cooperation between Nepal and India. Similarly, the potential achievements and new agendas that could be discussed during the Prime Minister's upcoming visit to India were also discussed in the meeting.

Discussions were held about seeking assistance from India for the reconstruction of areas affected by the BhoteKoshi flood. Sources from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs have stated that discussions were held to seek 500 million US dollars for rehabilitation and reconstruction. The main agenda of Prime Minister Balen's visit to India will be the rehabilitation and reconstruction of areas affected by the BhoteKoshi flood.

India has also promised to provide assistance in this regard. However, the amount of assistance and the method of providing it have not yet been decided. Discussions were also held about seeking assistance from India for the construction of various electricity transmission lines and other infrastructure projects within the country. Nepal is preparing a special proposal for this.

Sources claim that discussions were held regarding India providing grant assistance for the upgrade of the Siddharth Highway connecting India's Sunauli border to Pokhara.

Preparations are also underway to formally announce the operation of a train service from Ayodhya to Janakpur. Its testing was also conducted in Janakpur today. Preparations are also underway to jointly inaugurate the Police National Training Institute constructed with Indian assistance in Panauti, the Integrated Check Post in Bhairahawa, and the bridges built over the Darcula and Mahakali rivers. Information about all these matters was given to India's Foreign Secretary Misri during the meeting.

Discussions were held regarding the construction of the Dodhara Chandani Integrated Check Post, the Lower Arun Hydropower Project, and the Siliguri-Jhapa petroleum pipeline.

On the day of his arrival on Kartik 4, he held separate meetings with Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Minister for Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Biraj Bhakta Shrestha, and Minister for Physical Infrastructure and Transport Sunil Lamichhane.

In those meetings, the ministers expressed gratitude for the humanitarian and technical assistance provided by India after the Rasuwa-BhoteKoshi flood. Both sides discussed the progress being made in various new areas such as trade and commerce, development partnership, hydropower, physical infrastructure, border management, energy and people-to-people relations, as well as startups, digital connectivity, AI (Artificial Intelligence), and sports.

During the visit, Foreign Secretary Misri also interacted with members of the Nepal-India Parliamentary Friendship Group and members of the International Relations and Tourism Committee, as well as other parliamentarians. According to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, both countries reiterated their commitment to further elevate the multifaceted bilateral partnership.

India's Foreign Secretary Misri has returned after expressing India's commitment to always be ready to assist Nepal in its development construction. Secretary Misri also indicated that India will make some important announcements during Prime Minister Balen's visit to India. It is reported that officials from both countries are working on this.

title: Foreign Secretary Misri calls on Nepal’s PM Shah, discusses bilateral ties - Daily Pioneer
description: Foreign Secretary Misri calls on Nepal’s PM Shah, discusses bilateral ties  Daily Pioneer
publisher.title: Daily Pioneer
full_article:
Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri met Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah on Thursday and discussed issues of mutual interest and ways to further bolster bilateral cooperation in several areas.

The main purpose of the foreign secretary’s two-day visit to Nepal was to discuss Prime Minister Shah’s upcoming visit to India.

Foreign Secretary Misri called on PM Shah and conveyed to him greetings from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Embassy of India in Kathmandu said. “The discussion focused on the implementation of various bilateral initiatives, and possibilities for further enhancement of India-Nepal cooperation across domains, especially in the context of the forthcoming high-level visit,” it said in a post on X.

During the meeting at Singha Durbar, Foreign Secretary Misri said India has been making necessary preparations for the successful visit of Prime Minister Shah, the PM Office said in a statement here.

Prime Minister Shah expressed gratitude to the government of India for providing relief materials as the first responder after the devastating Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi flood and for providing assistance by sending a rescue team, the statement said.

He expressed gratitude to PM Modi for expressing solidarity through a telephone call at a time when Nepal was suffering from the disaster, it said. The Prime Minister also expressed interest in how Nepal can collaborate with India for the development of its sports sector.

Misri informed the Prime Minister that regular meetings of bilateral mechanisms of Nepal and India are being successfully conducted in the areas of energy, water resources, trade and transit and civil aviation. He also said that necessary preparations have been completed regarding the operation of the railway line between Ayodhya and Janakpur in Nepal. Prime Minister Shah is expected to visit India later this month. Misri, who arrived in Kathmandu on Wednesday, held delegation-level bilateral talks with Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai on the same day. He also separately met Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, and

Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha and discussed ongoing projects and initiatives as well as ways to enhance bilateral cooperation.

He also met Minister of Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal, who “shared his valuable insights on ways of enhancing bilateral cooperation, including in infrastructure and connectivity,” the Indian mission said. Nepal is important for India in the context of its overall strategic interests in the region, and leaders of the two countries have often noted the age-old “Roti Beti” relationship. Land-locked Nepal relies heavily on India for the transportation of goods and services.

Nepal’s access to the sea is through India, and it imports a predominant proportion of its requirements from and through India.

In May, the bilateral relations came under some unease following Shah’s remarks seeking involvement of China and the UK to address the border dispute between India and Nepal. New Delhi categorically rejected any role for third parties to resolve its boundary row with Nepal, saying the two countries have an established bilateral mechanism to deal with all aspects of the border issue.

title: Blood Pressure Prescriptions in Remote Nepal Reveal Sharp Gaps From WHO Standards - Bioengineer.org
description: Blood Pressure Prescriptions in Remote Nepal Reveal Sharp Gaps From WHO Standards  Bioengineer.org
publisher.title: Bioengineer.org
full_article:
Hypertensive outpatients at Karnali Academy of Health Sciences in Jumla, Nepal, are being treated with regimens that fall well short of World Health Organization prescribing standards, according to a cross-sectional study of 197 patients published in Pharmacology Research & Perspectives. The study found that only 34.4 percent of prescribed drugs were written by generic name against a WHO benchmark of 100 percent, and that prescriptions averaged 4.05 drugs per encounter, roughly double the WHO reference of fewer than 2.0. At the same time, the investigators judged the clinical selection of antihypertensive classes and the low rate of injection use to be appropriate for the setting.

The research team, working at the sole tertiary-care academic hospital in Karnali Province, enrolled adult patients aged 18 years and older who attended the outpatient department between June 2025 and December 2025, provided informed consent, and had been prescribed at least one antihypertensive medication. Patients receiving inpatient or emergency care were excluded, as were individuals with cognitive impairment, communication difficulties, or psychiatric conditions that would interfere with participation. The target sample was calculated with Cochran’s formula and adjusted for an anticipated 5 percent non-response rate, yielding 197 participants. Data were gathered prospectively: after consent, the researcher reviewed each patient’s outpatient prescription from the same visit and recorded details on a structured proforma, an approach designed to capture prescribing in real time and avoid recall bias.

The questionnaire used for data collection was developed in English after reviewing comparable published studies, then refined through a pre-test with 18 hypertensive outpatients, face validation by a pharmacy professor, and content review by medical experts and a statistician. Internal consistency measured by Cronbach’s alpha reached 0.70, which the authors describe as acceptable reliability. Responses were double-entered into Microsoft Excel 2019, cleaned for inconsistencies, and analyzed in IBM SPSS Statistics version 26.0 using descriptive statistics and chi-square tests, with p-values below 0.05 considered significant.

The participants were nearly evenly split by sex, with 51.3 percent male and 48.7 percent female, and the largest age group was 50 to 59 years at 23.9 percent of the sample. Mean age was 51.58 years. Education levels were modest: 39.1 percent had secondary schooling and 22.3 percent were illiterate. Housewives made up 37.6 percent of the cohort and farmers 28.4 percent, reflecting the agrarian economy of Karnali Province. A family history of hypertension was reported by 64.0 percent of participants. Lifestyle risk factors were striking: 94.4 percent reported high salt intake and 76.1 percent reported physical inactivity, while smoking stood at 17.8 percent and alcohol consumption at 23.4 percent.

Clinically, the cohort carried a heavy burden of established disease. Mean duration of hypertension was 7.97 years, mean systolic blood pressure was 155.91 mmHg, and mean diastolic pressure was 95.27 mmHg. Under the JNC-7 classification, 45.2 percent of patients fell into Stage 1 hypertension and 44.7 percent into Stage 2, with only one patient recording normal blood pressure. Overweight and obesity dominated the body mass index distribution, with 41.1 percent overweight and 33.5 percent distributed across the three obesity classes. Diabetes mellitus was the most common comorbidity at 22.8 percent, followed by dyslipidemia at 19.8 percent and chronic kidney disease at 11.7 percent.

Across the 799 drugs prescribed to the cohort, antihypertensives accounted for 44.7 percent, with other cardiovascular drugs and anti-ulcer agents each at 8.0 percent and lipid-lowering drugs at 7.8 percent. Among the 357 antihypertensive prescriptions, calcium channel blockers led at 32.8 percent, followed by angiotensin receptor blockers at 24.6 percent, diuretics at 19.3 percent, beta-blockers at 17.6 percent, and ACE inhibitors at just 5.6 percent. Amlodipine was the single most prescribed agent, representing 30.3 percent of antihypertensive prescriptions, ahead of telmisartan at 17.1 percent and atenolol at 13.4 percent. Within classes, amlodipine dominated the calcium channel blockers at 92.3 percent, telmisartan accounted for 69.3 percent of ARB prescriptions, and atenolol for 76.2 percent of beta-blockers.

Defined Daily Dose analysis based on the WHO Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification reinforced the same hierarchy. Amlodipine accumulated 3,390 DDDs, telmisartan 1,890, and atenolol 980, out of a cumulative total of 10,163 DDDs for all antihypertensive drugs in the study. Ramipril was a notable outlier, generating 1,140 DDDs from only 19 prescriptions, which the authors interpret as prescribing at longer durations or higher strengths. Telmisartan was prescribed at an average daily dose of 40 mg, exactly matching the WHO DDD for that drug.

Therapy patterns leaned toward combination treatment. Dual therapy was the most common regimen at 43.7 percent of patients, monotherapy accounted for 39.1 percent, triple therapy 15.7 percent, and quadruple therapy 1.5 percent, with a mean of 1.82 antihypertensive drugs per patient. The most frequent combinations were CCB plus ARB in dual therapy and CCB plus ARB plus diuretic in triple therapy. Chi-square analysis showed a highly significant association between therapy type and both JNC-7 stage and age group, each with p-values below 0.001: patients with Stage 2 hypertension and older patients were more likely to receive dual or polytherapy, while those with normal or prehypertensive readings predominantly received monotherapy. Gender showed no significant association with therapy pattern, with a p-value of 0.530, which the authors read as evidence that treatment decisions were not influenced by patient sex.

The WHO core prescribing indicators told a more mixed story. The average of 4.05 drugs per encounter substantially exceeded the reference standard of fewer than 2.0, a level of polypharmacy the authors attribute to the prevalence of comorbidities requiring multiple medications, the use of multiple antihypertensive agents, co-prescribing of gastroprotective agents such as pantoprazole, and adjunctive therapies including vitamins, supplements, and analgesics. Generic prescribing at 34.4 percent fell far below the 100 percent standard, and the authors identify this gap as likely the single most important modifiable factor in the study, noting that nearly two-thirds of prescriptions relied on brand names in a low-income setting where out-of-pocket costs matter. Antibiotic encounters at 14.2 percent and injection encounters at 7.6 percent fell within or below the WHO reference ranges of 20 to 26.8 percent and 13.4 to 24.1 percent respectively, which the authors interpret as reasonable antibiotic use and appropriate restraint with injections. Adherence to Nepal’s National List of Essential Medicines stood at 79.9 percent, below the 100 percent benchmark but described as moderate.

The authors conclude that antihypertensive prescribing at the hospital is clinically appropriate in drug selection and injection use but deviates significantly from WHO rational drug use standards in generic prescribing and polypharmacy, gaps they say directly increase patient costs and health risks. They caution that the study did not collect detailed individual-level information on dietary sodium intake, contraindications, previous treatment, adverse effects, renal function, electrolyte status, or prescriber preference, so the relatively low use of diuretics and ACE inhibitors cannot be judged inappropriate from prescription frequency alone. As a descriptive cross-sectional study from a single referral center in a remote district, the findings describe prescribing at one institution and time period rather than establishing causal relationships, but they offer a concrete baseline for interventions aimed at improving prescribing quality, affordability, and blood pressure control in underserved settings.
